title_ne: सुरक्षित मातृत्व तथा प्रजनन स्वास्थ्य अधिकार (पहिलो संशोधन) विधेयक, २०८३
summary:
The name of the bill is "Safe Motherhood and Reproductive Health Rights (First Amendment) Act, 2083" (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). The main purpose of this bill is to make maternity and reproductive health services safe, quality, easily available, and accessible in order to respect, protect, and fulfill women's rights to safe motherhood and reproductive health guaranteed by the Constitution of Nepal, and to make necessary provisions to address the declining population growth rate (Statement of Objects and Reasons, Page 1). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

Health institutions providing birthing services must provide birthing services through skilled health workers or, if unavailable, trained birth attendants (Section 4, Subsection 1, Page 1). Health institutions providing birthing services must not refuse to provide pregnancy services or birthing services under this Act to a pregnant woman due to financial or any other reasons (Section 4, Subsection 3, Page 1-2). Female employees working in government, non-governmental, or private organizations shall have the right to receive fully paid maternity leave of at least 6 months before or after childbirth (Section 7, Subsection 1, Page 2). If a pregnant woman gives birth to a stillborn child or if the child dies after birth, government, non-governmental, or private organizations must provide fully paid maternity leave of up to 98 days (Section 7, Subsection 2, Page 2). If the wife of a male employee working in a government, non-governmental, or private organization is giving birth, such employee must be provided with fully paid paternity care leave of up to 42 days before or after the wife gives birth (Section 7, Subsection 3, Page 2). Government, non-governmental, or private organizations must provide female employees working in their office who undergo complex surgery due to reproductive health morbidity with additional fully paid leave of at least 30 days before or after such surgery based on the opinion of a specialist doctor, but such leave shall not be granted for surgery performed during the maternity leave period taken under Subsection 1 of Section 13 (Section 8, Page 2). Every health institution must maintain organized records including the number of stillborn children and women who have had abortions (Section 5, Page 2). Health institutions must prioritize safe motherhood, emergency obstetric care, essential newborn care, and safe abortion care when providing services during a disaster, and may use prescribed innovative scientific technologies to provide such services (Section 16, Page 3-4).

Health institutions and health workers licensed under prevailing law must be listed as prescribed to provide safe abortion services (Section 11, Page 3). In normal pregnancy, health check-ups must be conducted at least four times and as needed according to the pregnant woman's health condition based on a doctor's recommendation (Section 3, Page 1).

Failing to refer to another health institution under Subsection 3 of Section 7 resulting in risk or harm is considered an offence (Section 13, Clause 1, Page 3). Committing or causing physical, mental, or sexual violence against women from pregnancy to the postpartum period contrary to Section 12a is considered an offence (Section 13, Clause 2, Page 3). Failing to provide priority services during a disaster under Subsection 1 of Section 29a is considered an offence (Section 13, Clause 3, Page 3). Performing or assisting in performing abortion except under specified conditions, causing abortion by coercing, threatening, coaxing, or enticing a pregnant woman, a child born alive during abortion dying immediately, abortion occurring while attempting to take a pregnant woman's life, or abortion occurring due to enmity against a pregnant woman is considered forced abortion (Section 10, Page 2-3). Anyone committing or causing to be committed these offences shall be punished with imprisonment for up to 6 months or a fine of up to Rs. 50 thousand or both (Section 14, Page 3). Who imposes the fine, the right to appeal, the time limit, and the court are not stated in the bill.
